findings.title: Call to isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments does not compile
findings.body: The only definition of `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` in the repository is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). A grep over all *.java files finds no no-arg overload. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()`, so the `services` module fails to compile and nothing in this PR can build or run. Pass the user instead: `if (context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()))`.

findings.title: `user != null` condition disables passkeys on the initial (unidentified) login
findings.body: Before this change, the passkey setup in `authenticate` ran only when the user was NOT yet identified, and `challenge(...)` on error ran only when `context.getUser() == null`. The new helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`, so `fillContextForm` is now called only when a user is already set. In a normal first login `context.getUser()` is null: `authenticate` takes the `else` branch (line 103) and `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(null)` at line 115 is false. The login page is then rendered without the conditional-UI attributes (challenge, rpId, `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI`). The same applies to the error path at line 137, because `getUser` clears the user before a failed username/password check. This breaks the main passkeys feature. The existing tests assert it, for example `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` (auto-login) and `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` (`//form[@id='webauth']` present and autocomplete `username webauthn` on the first page). It also looks inverted against the intended behaviour: the Organization test expects the webauthn form with the user already selected. The condition should allow `user == null`. For a set user it should probably check that the user has a passwordless credential (`user.credentialManager().isConfiguredFor(webauthnAuth.getCredentialType())`). That would also make the `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` comment true.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not cover a user without passkey
findings.body: The comment says passkeys should not be shown during re-authentication because "this user does not have passkey". The test actually disables passkeys at realm level (`setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`), so it only checks the realm switch. The case of a realm with passkeys enabled and a re-authenticating user who has no passkey is untested. The current helper (`user != null`) would show the passkey form to such a user. Add a test with passkeys enabled and a password-only user, or fix the comment. Separately, `catch (Exception nsee)` around `findElement`/`fail` is a weak pattern. `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, as used in the Organization test, is clearer.

findings.title: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication largely duplicates other tests
findings.body: The first half is a verbatim copy of `passwordLoginWithExternalKey` (lines 172-210), and the re-authentication half is covered again by `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey`. The shared setup could be pulled into a helper like `setPasswordlessPolicyForExternalKey`. The duplicated test also lengthens the already-slow browser suite.

findings.title: Missing @Override on overriding method
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the protected method added in `WebAuthnAuthenticator`, but has no `@Override`. Add it so a later signature change in the parent is caught at compile time.

contracts.action: Conditional-UI passkey form setup in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and challenge(error), gated by the new isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code: fillContextForm when user == null (authenticate, else-branch) and in challenge(error) only when context.getUser() == null
contracts.before_after: Before: passkeys were set up only for an unidentified user. After: the call is moved out of the else branch, but the helper requires user != null, so it now fires only for an identified user and never for the initial login.
contracts.visible_effect: The first login page loses the conditional-UI passkey form and auto-login; the re-authentication page gains it.
contracts.failure_mode: Existing passkey login tests would fail. The user cannot use passkeys on the normal login page.

contracts.action: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is called from badPasswordHandler and from the passkey error response
contracts.equivalent_path: Old inline block in badPasswordHandler, which called isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth(context)
contracts.before_after: The helper reads the same auth note (USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH) with the same Boolean.parseBoolean and sets the same two attributes (USERNAME_HIDDEN, REGISTRATION_DISABLED). The behaviour is equivalent, and it now also runs on passkey errors (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse), so the re-authentication form keeps the username hidden after a failed passkey.
contracts.visible_effect: After a failed passkey during re-authentication, the form still hides the username and registration link.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. The note is removed in the user==null branch of authenticate, so stale state is not carried into a fresh login.

contracts.action: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm now asks shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators; the conditional-UI authenticator overrides it to false
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous `if (user != null)` in the same method, which is still the default for the 2FA WebAuthnAuthenticator
contracts.before_after: Before: with a user set, conditional UI would load allowed authenticators and return null (no form) if the user had none. After: conditional UI never does this, so a user without passwordless keys no longer short-circuits to null. SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS is already false via WebAuthnPasswordlessAuthenticator.
contracts.visible_effect: Re-authentication page renders the passkeys form for any user with a set user (for the current helper).

summary: The PR does not compile and, once fixed, still breaks passkeys on the normal login page. `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition takes a `UserModel`. The new helper in `UsernamePasswordForm.java:161` also requires `user != null`. That turns passkey setup off for the initial unidentified login, which is the main use case and the one existing tests exercise. It enables passkeys only for re-authentication. Other findings are test duplication, a test whose comment doesn't match what it checks, and a missing `@Override`. I did not run or build anything, only read the code.
